before: The architecture had converged on SOURCE → HOLD → TURN → TRACE → RETURN, but the loop existed mainly as shorthand across FIELD/INTERPHASE laws and was not yet a concise human/agent operational contract with explicit entry/exit conditions.
after: A single active protocol now defines exact entry/exit conditions, concrete examples, EFFECT→RELEASE compatibility, PASS/FAIL/INDETERMINATE evidence semantics, stop rules, agent handoff packet and next:NONE after RETURN. FIELD footer and system map link to it without enlarging the primary action surface.

residue.user_rule: What exactly? → Hold one thing → Make one bounded move → Prove what changed → Write what came back.
residue.agent_rule: One addressed object/focus; ≤3 native moves; one TURN; EFFECT requires native RELEASE; TRACE never creates authority; RETURN sets next:NONE.
unknowns: No claim that every existing route has yet adopted this protocol internally; it is the default control contract and handoff grammar, not a silent rewrite of host-native logic.
